The House of Hohenzollern. Originating in Swabia, the Hohenzollerns acquired the Margraviate of Brandenburg in the fifteenth century, which became the kernel of Prussian power. Through military genius, administrative reform, and aggressive statecraft, they transformed Prussia into Europe's mightiest power in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

Frederick the Great, who reigned from 1740 to 1786, transformed Prussia into a major European power through military victories, enlightened reforms, and the conquest of Silesia from Austria. He developed the Prussian military system—disciplined, efficient, and feared throughout Europe. Under the Hohenzollerns, the army was the state and the state was the army.

Otto von Bismarck, serving as Chancellor from 1862 to 1890, unified the fragmented German states through war and diplomacy, creating the German Empire in 1871 under King William I. Kaiser Wilhelm II reigned from 1888 to 1918, the last German emperor. He presided over imperial expansion, naval rivalry with Britain, and Germany's ill-fated plunge into World War I. When the empire faced military defeat and revolution, he abdicated in November 1918, ending the dynasty and ushering in the Weimar Republic.
